title: Derived change of rings along a map of ring sheaves is left adjoint to restriction of scalars, with normalized unit and transposes
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site and $\varphi:\mathcal O\to\mathcal O'$ a morphism of sheaves of commutative rings on $\mathcal C$. Use the abelian categories of sheaves of $\mathcal O$- and $\mathcal O'$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], their unbounded derived categories $D(\mathcal O)$, $D(\mathcal O')$ with localizations $Q$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], restriction of scalars $\operatorname{Res}_\varphi$ [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars] and the change of rings $-\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal O'$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Then $\operatorname{Res}_\varphi$ is exact, so applying it termwise defines $\operatorname{Res}_\varphi:D(\mathcal O')\to D(\mathcal O)$. Let $L\varphi^*=-\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O}\mathcal O':D(\mathcal O)\to D(\mathcal O')$ be the derived change of rings of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], computed on K-flat complexes with flat terms [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules, lem-pc-kflat-resolution] through the canonical isomorphism $c_P:L\varphi^*(QP)\cong Q(P\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal O')$. Then $L\varphi^*$ is left adjoint to $\operatorname{Res}_\varphi$: there are bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O')}(L\varphi^*K,H)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O)}(K,\operatorname{Res}_\varphi H),$$
natural in $K\in D(\mathcal O)$ and $H\in D(\mathcal O')$, normalized on representatives as follows. Let $P$ be a K-flat complex of $\mathcal O$-modules with flat terms. (1) Under $c_P$, the unit at $QP$ is the class of the termwise map $P\to\operatorname{Res}_\varphi(P\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal O')$, $x\mapsto x\otimes1$. (2) For a complex $H$ of $\mathcal O'$-modules and a morphism of complexes $g:P\to\operatorname{Res}_\varphi H$, the adjunct of $Q(g)$ is, under $c_P$, the class of the morphism of complexes $P\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal O'\to H$, $x\otimes a\mapsto a\,g(x)$. In particular, if $g$ is a quasi-isomorphism, the counit at $QH$ is this class composed with $c_P$ and the inverse of $L\varphi^*(Q(g))$. No flatness of $\varphi$ and no boundedness is assumed.

proof.text: Apply the general-site ordinary coefficient adjunction to obtain exact restriction and the normalized ordinary adjunction for the prescribed E.
Apply the derived Hom comparison to the supplied universal pair to obtain d and its representative Hom identity.

Presentations with the same object and map equations are equal by Functor.ext. Transfer the K-flat universal pair supplied by derivedChangeOfRingsIndependentCoefficients to E. Uniqueness of left derived functors gives a natural isomorphism intertwining counits; its component and the supplied K-flat counit are invertible, so epsilon_P is invertible.

Evaluate the representative Hom identity at the identity of E_h(P). Expand homEquiv as unit followed by the right functor map and cancel the exact-restriction comparison isomorphism. This gives the required unit normalization. Apply the same formula to the ordinary inverse adjunct of g and use both inverse laws of the Hom equivalences to obtain the required transpose. Finally homEquiv_counit writes this inverse adjunct as LF(q) followed by counit. If Qh(g) is invertible, so is q and LF(q); cancel LF(q) to get the displayed counit formula.
